Inequality gaps from the official estimates

Source: R/inequality.R
bdhs_inequality_official.Rd

Computes the inequality measures of bdhs_inequality() from the official DHS estimates by wealth quintile (bdhs_official()), for every round with such estimates. These are point estimates only (the official tables carry no covariances). The measures follow from the group values \(\mu_k\) and the weighted denominators \(p_k\) of the five quintiles: difference \(\mu_5 - \mu_1\), ratio \(\mu_5 / \mu_1\), sii and rii from the weighted (least squares and log-link) regression of \(\mu_k\) on the ridit \(R_k\), which equals the individual-level regression because the ridit is constant within groups, ci \(= 2 \sum_k p_k \mu_k R_k / \mu - 1\) and eci \(= 4 \mu C\) (for percentages, with \(\mu\) as a proportion). Official values are rounded, so the measures are approximate.

Usage

bdhs_inequality_official(
  indicator,
  survey = NULL,
  measures = .inequality_measures,
  period = NULL
)

Arguments

indicator

A DHS indicator id (e.g. "RH_DELA_C_CSC") or a bdhs indicator id with a DHS equivalent (e.g. "rh_del_csection").

survey

Optional survey references; NULL uses every round.

measures

Measures to compute (see bdhs_inequality()).

period

Reference period of the official values, as in the by_variable_label column of bdhs_official(preferred = FALSE) (e.g. "Three years preceding the survey"). NULL (default) uses the period that bdhs computes for a bdhs indicator id (so the result is comparable with bdhs_inequality() on the microdata), and the DHS headline (preferred) value for a DHS id.

Value

A tibble of class bdhs_inequality with columns survey_id, indicator, label, by ("Wealth quintile"), measure, measure_label, estimate, lowest, highest and n_groups; se, ci_low and ci_high are NA.

References

Barros AJD, Victora CG (2013). Measuring coverage in MNCH: determining and interpreting inequalities in coverage of maternal, newborn, and child health interventions. PLoS Medicine 10(5): e1001390.

Erreygers G (2009). Correcting the concentration index. Journal of Health Economics 28(2): 504-515.

Kakwani N, Wagstaff A, van Doorslaer E (1997). Socioeconomic inequalities in health: measurement, computation, and statistical inference. Journal of Econometrics 77(1): 87-103.

Wagstaff A, Paci P, van Doorslaer E (1991). On the measurement of inequalities in health. Social Science & Medicine 33(5): 545-557.

Examples

bdhs_inequality_official("RH_DELA_C_CSC")
#> # BDHS inequality: RH_DELA_C_CSC by Wealth quintile | BD2000DHS, BD2004DHS, BD2007DHS, BD2011DHS, BD2014DHS, BD2017DHS, BD2022DHS
#> # A tibble: 42 × 13
#>    survey_id indicator   label by    measure measure_label estimate    se ci_low
#>    <chr>     <chr>       <chr> <chr> <chr>   <chr>            <dbl> <dbl>  <dbl>
#>  1 BD2000DHS RH_DELA_C_… Deli… Weal… differ… Difference (…  11.2       NA     NA
#>  2 BD2000DHS RH_DELA_C_… Deli… Weal… ratio   Ratio (highe…  17         NA     NA
#>  3 BD2000DHS RH_DELA_C_… Deli… Weal… sii     Slope index …  11.2       NA     NA
#>  4 BD2000DHS RH_DELA_C_… Deli… Weal… rii     Relative ind… 140.        NA     NA
#>  5 BD2000DHS RH_DELA_C_… Deli… Weal… ci      Concentratio…   0.588     NA     NA
#>  6 BD2000DHS RH_DELA_C_… Deli… Weal… eci     Erreygers co…   0.0711    NA     NA
#>  7 BD2004DHS RH_DELA_C_… Deli… Weal… differ… Difference (…  19.3       NA     NA
#>  8 BD2004DHS RH_DELA_C_… Deli… Weal… ratio   Ratio (highe…  97.5       NA     NA
#>  9 BD2004DHS RH_DELA_C_… Deli… Weal… sii     Slope index …  19.8       NA     NA
#> 10 BD2004DHS RH_DELA_C_… Deli… Weal… rii     Relative ind… 432.        NA     NA
#> # ℹ 32 more rows
#> # ℹ 4 more variables: ci_high <dbl>, lowest <chr>, highest <chr>,
#> #   n_groups <int>
bdhs_inequality_official("rh_del_facility", survey = c(2004, 2022),
                         measures = c("difference", "ratio"))
